subject: Urgent: Adrift Retail throughput & latency incident — analysis and action plan
messages:
From: Maya Fowler <maya@adriftretail.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-29T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: High latency & 5xx spike impacting checkout volumes

Hi Aditya,

We saw a sustained latency increase and an accompanying 5xx error spike starting around 21:30 UTC yesterday and lasting into early morning local time. This affected checkout throughput on our busiest SKU groups; we estimate ~18% drop in completed checkouts during peak. Our ops team is seeing timeouts from the inference endpoint and high tail latency from 3-6s on requests that normally complete <200ms.

This is causing customer-facing failures and we need exec-level visibility and a concrete remediation timeline. Can you confirm:

- Do you have a preliminary root cause?
- What immediate mitigations can you apply to stabilize throughput?
- Will we be eligible for SLA credit for this outage window?

Attaching a short summary from our logs (see ProcLog snippet) and chart exports. Please escalate internally and share next steps by EOD. We’re standing by for a bridge if helpful.

Thanks,
Maya Fowler
Head of Platform Engineering
Adrift Retail, Inc.

Attachment: adrift_proc_logs_excerpt.txt (text)
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
To: Maya Fowler <maya@adriftretail.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-29T09:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: High latency & 5xx spike impacting checkout volumes

Maya — thanks for the note and the log excerpts, and I’m really sorry you hit this. I’ve escalated to our on-call infra/serving team and looped in Kimberly and Sergio to lead a rapid analysis.

Immediate items we’re doing now:
- Triage call: 10:00 PT / 17:00 UTC (I’ll send a calendar invite if that time works)
- Short-term mitigation: we can route traffic to a lower-capacity but more conservative model variant for the hot SKU routes to reduce tail latency (risk: slightly different output distribution)
- Collecting detailed perf counters & KV cache hit rates for the window you reported

Proposed mutual action plan for the next 48 hours (high-level):
1) Today: triage + temporary traffic routing + confirm mitigation effect (owner: Sergio)
2) 24h: initial incident analysis + prioritized list of fixes (owner: Kimberly)
3) 72h: deliver written incident analysis and action items, including ETA for permanent fixes and test plan (owner: Laura)

Can you confirm whether the 10:00 PT time works for your team and share a point of contact for procurement/contract questions if SLA calculation is required? I’ll follow up with an internal readout and the bridge link.

—Aditya

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Maya Fowler <maya@adriftretail.com>
Cc: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-30T14:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: High latency & 5xx spike impacting checkout volumes — draft analysis and corrective actions

Hi all,

Following the triage and data pulls, I’m attaching a short incident analysis (PDF) and a set of corrective actions we propose. Key findings (summary):

- Root cause: a combination of a regression in batch-sizing heuristics in our serving runtime (deployed 2026-08-25) and a correlated KV-cache churn for long-tail customer prefixes. At high concurrency this produced underfilled batches and frequent memory pressure reclamations, which drove up tail latency and triggered transient 5xxs.

- Impact window: 2026-08-28T21:20:00Z — 2026-08-29T03:15:00Z (observed by Adrift traffic patterns)

- Metrics: peak p95 latency jumped from ~180ms to ~2.9s; 5xx rate increased from 0.02% to ~1.7% during the window; checkout throughput for hot SKUs reduced by ~18% at peak.

Immediate corrective actions (48h):
- Roll back the batch-sizing change in the serving runtime (owner: Kimberly, ETA: 6h)
- Enable conservative batching for Adrift routes with a temporary per-customer override (owner: Sergio, ETA: 3h)
- Increase KV cache retention for the affected route to reduce churn (owner: Sergio, ETA: 12h)
- Add circuit-breaker thresholds and automatic fallback to the verified model variant for the affected endpoints (owner: Laura, ETA: 24h)

Medium-term remediation (2–4 weeks):
- Add regression test for batch-sizing behavior under recorded Adrift traffic profile (owner: Eng-Test, ETA: 2w)
- Improve telemetry for per-customer KV churn and low-fill batch alerts (owner: Observability, ETA: 3w)

Deliverables included with this email:
- adrift_incident_analysis_v1.pdf (attached) — includes charts and annotated timelines
- tokenized-throughput-charts.png (attached) — visual of throughput drop and latency tails

Next steps I need from Adrift:
- Confirmation to proceed with the temporary routing/fallback today
- Any constraints around model variant changes (e.g., regulatory labels, scoring differences you cannot accept)

I’ll circulate a clean final RCA once we hit the 72h checkpoint with tests and rollouts planned.

Regards,
Kimberly Park
Sr. Ops Manager — Serving Runtime
kimberly.park@redwood.com

Attachment: adrift_incident_analysis_v1.pdf (PDF)
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
To: Maya Fowler <maya@adriftretail.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Procurement Team <procure@adriftretail.com>
Date: 2026-08-30T16:00:00-07:00
Subject: Final: Incident analysis summary, commitments, and next steps (Adrift Retail)

Maya — thank you for the quick sync earlier. Per Kimberly’s analysis attached, here’s the agreed plan and commitments from Redwood: 

1) Stabilization (complete) — rolled back the batch-sizing heuristic and enabled conservative batching + increased KV retention for your routes. We observed p95 latency return to baseline in the Canary within 30 minutes; we’ve kept the conservative overrides for 48 hours while we validate.

2) Short-term safety net (24h) — added automatic fallback to the verified model variant for the checkout endpoints; will maintain the fallback policy for 72h and then evaluate rollback. Owner: Laura Bennett.

3) Permanent remediation (2–4 weeks) — testing and telemetry improvements to prevent recurrence; build and schedule regression tests to be completed by 2026-09-20. Owner: Kimberly Park.

Operational notes and timelines:
- We will provide a final written RCA and test results by 2026-09-01.
- If you confirm acceptance of the conservative routing, we’ll keep the change live and backfill you with updated charts every 6 hours for the first 48 hours.
- For SLA accounting: I’ve opened a support billing ticket and looped in our finance ops; we’ll calculate the window and provide an SLA credit estimate within 5 business days. HubSpot deal link included below.

Attachments: adrift_incident_analysis_v1.pdf, tokenized-throughput-charts.png
Related: https://drive.redwood.com/drive/folders/ADR-197/incident-analysis

Please reply with an OK to proceed or any constraints you want to discuss. I’m available for another short call if you’d like to run the remediation plan with your ops team.

Thanks — Aditya
